title: The Atmosphere Admonition Through Atmospheric Events And The Result I Believe In Allah

questions.question: What are the people being told to do at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: They are told to raise their heads and notice the amazing works happening above them.

questions.question: Why does the passage say people should look up at these events in the sky?
questions.answer: Because these events show the power and actions of the One who wants to be known.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about being “left on your own”?
questions.answer: It teaches that people are not without care, and the events in the sky are not without control either.

questions.question: According to the passage, do the events in the atmosphere happen for no reason or for a purpose?
questions.answer: They happen for a purpose.

questions.question: Who gives each event its job in the passage?
questions.answer: A supremely wise planner gives each one its task.

questions.question: Which parts of the atmosphere are named as giving a strong witness to the truth?
questions.answer: The winds, the rain coming down, and the management of events in the sky.

questions.question: After hearing this witness, what does the traveler say?
questions.answer: He says that he believes in Allah.

questions.question: What idea about Allah is strongly supported by the atmosphere in this passage?
questions.answer: That Allah truly exists and is One.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the way the atmosphere gives its witness?
questions.answer: It gives a broad, complete, and clearly seen witness through the order and control within it.

questions.question: What do the sky events show about the Being behind them?
questions.answer: They show that He is active, powerful, and makes Himself known through His works.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the sky events: random or guided?
questions.answer: They are guided and managed.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the role of each event in the atmosphere?
questions.answer: Each one is made to carry out its own special duty.

questions.question: What kind of ruler or manager is in charge of these events?
questions.answer: One who is perfectly wise in arranging and directing them.

questions.question: Name three things in the passage that help form this testimony from the atmosphere.
questions.answer: The winds, the falling rain, and the ordering of what happens in the air.

questions.question: What effect does this testimony have on the traveler?
questions.answer: It leads him to faith in Allah.

questions.question: What important truth does the traveler understand from the atmosphere’s witness?
questions.answer: He understands Allah’s necessary existence and unity.

questions.question: Why is the testimony of the atmosphere called observable in the passage?
questions.answer: Because its order, control, and actions can be seen in the world.

questions.question: What are they invited to notice instead?
questions.answer: They are invited to notice the wonderful actions taking place in the sky.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the sky events having an owner?
questions.answer: It teaches that these events belong to a master who controls them.

questions.question: What does having a “master and a purpose” tell us about these events?
questions.answer: It tells us they are not meaningless but planned and useful.

questions.question: How are the tasks of the sky events described?
questions.answer: Each one has its own particular duty to fulfill.

questions.question: What qualities are shown by the one who directs these events?
questions.answer: Wisdom, power, and careful control.

questions.question: What combined signs lead the traveler to his conclusion?
questions.answer: The movement of the winds, the sending down of rain, and the running of events in the atmosphere.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveler reach from these signs?
questions.answer: He reaches belief in Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say the whole atmosphere testifies to?
questions.answer: It testifies to Allah’s existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What simple action does the passage first ask a person to take?
questions.answer: It asks the person to look up.

questions.question: What is special about the deeds the person is asked to notice?
questions.answer: They are amazing signs of great power and action.

questions.question: What does the passage say about people and sky events being on their own?
questions.answer: Neither people nor those events are left without care and direction.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the world?
questions.answer: It tells us the world is run with order and intention.

questions.question: How is each event in the atmosphere treated in the passage?
questions.answer: Each one is assigned a certain job.

questions.question: What title best fits the one managing these events: careless ruler, wise disposer, or weak watcher?
questions.answer: Wise disposer.

questions.question: What parts of nature are especially mentioned as bearing witness?
questions.answer: The winds, the rain, and the other happenings in the atmosphere.

questions.question: What does the traveler do after understanding their witness?
questions.answer: He declares his faith in Allah.

questions.question: What truth about Allah is stated in the traveler’s understanding?
questions.answer: That Allah necessarily exists and is one.

questions.question: Why is this witness from the atmosphere powerful?
questions.answer: Because it is wide-reaching, well-ordered, and clearly seen.

questions.question: In the passage, what are people encouraged to notice above them?
questions.answer: They are encouraged to notice the marvelous events in the sky.

questions.question: What do these events help reveal?
questions.answer: They help reveal the One who controls them and wants to be known.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the purpose of these events?
questions.answer: It says they are made to serve meaningful purposes.

questions.question: How many of the sky events are said to have jobs?
questions.answer: Every one of them has its own task.

questions.question: What does that suggest about how the atmosphere works?
questions.answer: It works with careful planning and order.

questions.question: Which natural processes are said to give testimony together?
questions.answer: The arranging of the winds, the sending of rain, and the governing of the atmosphere.

questions.question: What two big truths about Allah are supported by this testimony?
questions.answer: His real existence and His unity.

questions.question: Is the atmosphere’s testimony hidden or noticeable? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: It is noticeable because its orderly signs can be observed.

questions.question: What does the passage tell a neglectful person to do with his head and eyes?
questions.answer: It tells him to lift his head and look carefully.

questions.question: What is he supposed to see when he looks up?
questions.answer: He is supposed to see astonishing signs of power and action.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about whether sky events happen by themselves?
questions.answer: They do not happen by themselves.

questions.question: If they do not happen by themselves, what does the passage say they have?
questions.answer: They have a master and a clear purpose.

questions.question: What is true about the job of each event in the atmosphere?
questions.answer: Each one is directed to carry out a specific duty.

questions.question: What does the passage call the one who directs all this?
questions.answer: A most wise manager.

questions.question: What three atmospheric matters does the traveler hear as a testimony?
questions.answer: The ordering of the winds, the falling of the rains, and the running of events in the air.

questions.question: What statement of faith does the traveler make at the end of this section?
questions.answer: He says, “I believe in Allah.”

questions.question: What does the atmosphere, with all that is in it, point to according to the passage?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole target passage?
questions.answer: The atmosphere and its events are orderly signs that lead the traveler to believe in Allah.
